body.estimand_functional: For every feasible positive fixed-count sample-and-assign design, including an optional unassigned remainder, \[\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}=\sup_{Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)}\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y}\mid Y)\}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad C^{\mathsf T}WC\in\mathcal R_K.\]

sampling_model.design: The headline design is uniform over assignments with prespecified positive arm counts \(n_a\geq1\) and an optional unassigned count \(n_{\mathrm u}=N-\sum_a n_a\geq0\). Balanced complete randomization, with \(K\mid N\), \(n_a=N/K\), and \(n_{\mathrm u}=0\), is retained as an exact subdomain. The separate kernel problem continues to range only over laws in \(\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{bal}}_{N,K}\), so the general uniform-design and balanced-kernel domains are not conflated.
sampling_model.units: The \(N\) units and all \(K\) potential outcomes per unit are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling. An unassigned label records units omitted from the experimental sample without making the potential outcomes random.
sampling_model.treatment: The assignment vector \(Z\) is the sole random object. Under the headline law it uniformly chooses disjoint arm samples of sizes \(n_a\), leaving \(n_{\mathrm u}\) units unassigned; under the separate nonexchangeable balanced analysis it follows the known admissible law \(p\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every reported arm has known positive probability \(n_a/N>0\). The unassigned probability \(n_{\mathrm u}/N\) may be zero, and no outcome mean is defined for the unassigned label.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The structural endpoint conditions on the full armwise empirical marginals \(F\) and is therefore an oracle finite-population completion result. Aronow, Green, and Lee's Equation (2) and Lemma 1 supply the exact two-arm oracle benchmark; their asymptotic analysis of bounds estimated from observed marginal samples is not claimed here.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Equation (2) gives the exact finite-population difference-in-means variance with treated, control, and unsampled counts, and Lemma 1 gives the sharp comonotone covariance endpoint from known marginals.
An integer program computes a worst-case copula for broad designs and estimators.
Multi-marginal optimal transport gives exact identified sets for general quadratic cross-world objectives.
The design-based framework permits arbitrary multi-arm contrast matrices.
Supermodular expectations are monotone in concordance for distributions with fixed marginals.
The identity permutation is optimal for a Robinson similarity and dissimilarity when one is Toeplitz.
Isotone imputation converges to a least-favourable two-arm limiting experiment.

body.tldr: Under uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign randomization with arbitrary positive arm counts and any nonnegative unassigned remainder, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) exactly when \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian. The off-diagonal completion objective and exact \(2/N\) regret identity do not depend on the arm counts. The result includes the full finite two-arm Aronow--Green--Lee oracle design, while balanced complete randomization remains an exact subdomain for the six-unit audits and the separate balanced-kernel copositivity theory. For admissible balanced covariance tensors, finite exact recognition remains available for exact real-algebraic inputs; polynomial-time recognition and the minimal complete witness alphabet remain open.

project_justification.gap: Aronow, Green, and Lee give the sharp two-arm oracle endpoint for a random sample assigned with fixed treated and control counts, while generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact multi-arm contrast-geometry boundary that is uniform over unequal positive arm counts and optional unsampled units. On the realizable nonexchangeable balanced-kernel domain, the remaining gap is polynomial-time recognition or a faithful hardness result, together with a minimal-alphabet separating certificate.
project_justification.niche: The object is neither a generic transport solver nor another conservative covariance estimator. It is a design-computable graph-Laplacian cone for every uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign design, a sharper classification for joint covariance dominance, and, on the distinct balanced nonexchangeable domain, an exact cut-copositivity representation modulo common unit relabelling.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the unequal-count sample-and-assign covariance decomposition, proves that its completion-dependent term is count-free, and uses finite rearrangement plus isolated binary witnesses to obtain the graph-Laplacian equivalence, exact regret, and Loewner classification without balance or divisibility restrictions. It recovers the full finite Aronow--Green--Lee oracle design with the normalization \(S_{ab}=N\sigma_{ab}^{(N)}/(N-1)\), retains exact balanced six-unit audits, and keeps the general balanced-kernel copositivity theorem and its computational residual questions on their original subdomain.

body.related_work: Aronow, Green, and Lee study \(N\geq4\) fixed units, sample \(n_{\mathrm s}\) without replacement, assign \(m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) to treatment and \(n_{\mathrm s}-m_{\mathrm t}\geq2\) to control, and leave \(N-n_{\mathrm s}\) unsampled. Their Equation (2) is exactly the two-arm specialization of the fixed-count covariance identity after \(S_{ab}=N\sigma_{ab}^{(N)}/(N-1)\), and their Lemma 1 supplies the sharp comonotone oracle endpoint. This finite known-marginal equivalence is distinct from their subsequent asymptotic theory for estimated bounds. Imbens and Menzel use the same isotone completion for a least-favourable limiting experiment. Zhao and Ding supply arbitrary-contrast complete-randomization covariance algebra but do not optimize its unidentified cross-arm terms. Tchen's supermodular-order theorem agrees with the pairwise rearrangement mechanism, while the proof here is finite and direct. Gao, Ge, and Qian formulate general quadratic cross-world extrema as multi-marginal transport, and Brennan et al. compute generalized causal-bootstrap completions by integer programming. The separate general-kernel theorem remains restricted to covariance tensors in the exact finite moment-polytope image of balanced assignment laws and gives a finite cut-copositivity characterization. Laurent and Seminaroti's Robinson--Toeplitz result is a sufficient identity-optimal class for a two-matrix quadratic assignment problem, not the necessary-and-sufficient or polynomial recognition result sought here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The graph-Laplacian certificate is an oracle completion theorem for a prespecified scalar covariance loss \(W\); it does not estimate unknown armwise marginals and does not turn the endpoint into a sharp matrix-valued covariance bound. Except for a rescaled pairwise contrast, no single common-rank completion dominates every linear combination simultaneously. The full Aronow--Green--Lee finite design and sharp known-marginal endpoint are recovered, but their estimated-bound asymptotics are not reproved. For general nonexchangeable balanced kernels, the copositivity theorem is exhaustive rather than scalable: it enumerates factorially many relabellings and arm permutations and exponentially many supports, and strict witnesses may use as many as \(N\) ordered levels per arm.
body.honest_scope: The uniform fixed-count cone theorem follows from exact assignment-indicator moments, the count-free cross-arm covariance coefficient, a finite rearrangement proof, and a contrast-geometry necessity construction. Its domain permits arbitrary positive arm counts and a nonnegative unassigned remainder; balanced complete randomization is only a retained specialization. The two-arm statement recovers the Aronow--Green--Lee oracle variance formula and sharp comonotone endpoint, not their asymptotic estimated-bound results. The six-unit propositions remain balanced finite audits. The general balanced-kernel contribution remains the proved finite cut-copositivity equivalence and, for exact real-algebraic inputs, a terminating exact algorithm. No polynomial runtime, hardness classification, binary completeness, or minimal-alphabet theorem is claimed.
body.interpretation: For any uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign experiment, a practitioner can ignore the unequal diagonal sampling coefficients when comparing potential-outcome completions: only the common term \(-N^{-1}\sum_{a,b}H_{ab}S_{ab}\) varies. Nonpositive off-diagonal entries of \(C^{\mathsf T}WC\) certify one-sort least-favourable completion, while a positive entry identifies two arms on which a finite binary reversal strictly improves the loss. This conclusion and the \(2/N\) regret identity are unchanged by unequal allocation or unsampled units. Matrix-valued conservativeness remains much rarer, and the nonexchangeable balanced-design analogue remains a finite copositivity problem rather than part of the generalized uniform design.
